messages:
acme_admin: Hey team — rolled our enterprise SSO yesterday. Affected user reports they can see the project in the console but all API requests using their API key return 403. Example curl below. Can we triage?

acme_admin: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/our-prod-project` --> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

ana_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share the user email and example API key prefix (first 8 chars)? Also, do they authenticate to the console via SSO or local account?

acme_admin: user email is sarah+eng@acme.com, api key prefix `sk_live_1a2b3c4d`. She signs into console via SSO now. Before SSO she used a local account and had Project Editor on the project.

ana_support: Thanks. Quick suspicion: when SCIM provisioning ran we may have provisioned a separate SSO-backed user record instead of linking to the legacy account, so the API key is still owned by the old (now-orphaned) identity. In the UI you might still see the role because of the old record being visible to some caches.

acme_admin: Hmm that would explain it — I can see two entries for that email in org members list: one shows source=legacy, one shows source=okta-scim. They both show sarah+eng but different internal IDs. Is that expected?

jordan_eng: This matches a known edge case: duplicate identities after SCIM enabled on an org where users had local accounts. API keys are bound to the account id that created them. If provisioning created a new identity, calls using the old key will 403 because that account no longer has the project binding.

jordan_eng: Short-term workaround: rotate the API key (generate a new key from the SSO-linked account) or ask us to rebind the existing key to the SSO identity. We can rebind if you provide the org_id and the key suffix (last 8 chars) and confirm authorization.

ana_support: @acme_admin can you confirm org_id and the last 8 chars of the key? Also paste the two member lines you see (redact IDs) — e.g. `sarah+eng@acme.com (legacy, id: 0xabc...)` and `sarah+eng@acme.com (okta-scim, id: 0xdef...)`.

acme_admin: Org id `org_9z8y7x`, key suffix `3c4d5e6f`. Member lines: `sarah+eng@acme.com (legacy, id: 72f1a9)` and `sarah+eng@acme.com (okta-scim, id: d9c0b2)`. I can rotate if needed but would prefer not to break dependent deploys tonight.

jordan_eng: Understood. We can rebind the existing key to the SCIM identity (non-disruptive). I'll open an internal migration job and ask infra to verify audit trail. Can you confirm which project(s) need the key access?

acme_admin: `our-prod-project` and `integration-tests`

jordan_eng: Thanks. We'll attempt a non-destructive migration: map legacy account -> scim account and move API key ownership. Steps I will take: 1) validate key suffix and org_id 2) snapshot current bindings 3) reassign key owner 4) run quick smoke curl to confirm 200. If anything looks off we'll rollback.

scim-bot: SCIM provisioning job #98765 completed at 2024-11-02T03:12:10Z. 1 user created, 12 updated, 0 removed.

ana_support: One more ask for audit: please confirm the timestamp when Sarah first signed in via SSO (we'll match login events).

acme_admin: She first signed in 2024-11-02T03:05:00Z per our IdP logs.

jordan_eng: Good. I'll proceed with creating the internal ticket and tag infra on the migration. I'll update this thread with the ticket id and the smoke test results. ETA ~ 2 hours.

ana_support: Also, after we fix this we'll recommend running our SCIM user-linking script to reconcile remaining duplicates (prevents recurrence). We'll share steps in the ticket. :thumbsup:

acme_admin: Awesome, thanks. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
